Isotonic regression.

Source: R/inferDivergenceTimes.R
model_iso.Rd

This function uses the relationship between cumulative branch length and time to infer the divergence times of ancestral nodes that have only the cumulative branch length.

Usage

model_iso(known, unknown, x_grid = NULL)

Arguments

known

Nodes with both divergence time (column divergenceTime) and cumulative branch length (column cumBranchLen).

unknown

Nodes with only cumulative branch length (column cumBranchLen; column divergenceTime is NA).

x_grid

Optional parameter with extra points beyond those with unknown divergence times. These can be used, for example, to plot or check accuracy over a wider range.

Value

A list with 2 types of predictions: 1. pred_unknown: predictions for nodes in the path with unknown divergence time; 2. pred_grid: predictions for the extra points passed in x_grid.

Details

The relationship between cumulative branch length and time is inferred with Isotonic regression. Isotonic regression is the technique of fitting a free-form line to a sequence of observations such that the fitted line is non-decreasing (or non-increasing) everywhere, and lies as close to the observations as possible.
